questions.stem: In any emergency the first priority is:
options: Protecting life
Saving the catch
Finding who is to blame
Saving the paint

questions.stem: In an engine room fire you should shut off:
options: The bilge and deck wash pumps
Radio and navigation lights
Fuel and ventilation
Fire pump and hydrants

questions.stem: If the other vessel's bow plugs a hole in your hull after collision you should:
options: Abandon ship straight away
Pull away at once to look at the damage
Keep it there until you can assess
Go ahead on your engine to free her
questions.explanation: It may be keeping you afloat.

questions.stem: After a grounding you should first:
options: Go full astern to get off at once
Check people and damage and sound the bilges
Pump out the tanks to lighten her
Call the owner before doing anything

questions.stem: When you abandon the vessel you should if possible:
options: Take off your lifejacket so you can swim
Board the liferaft dry and stay with it
Swim for shore if you can see the land
Split up so rescuers find someone sooner

questions.stem: A master who hears a Mayday must:
options: Wait for the Coast Guard to call
Render assistance so far as it is safe
Help only if the casualty is nearby
Pass the call on and keep fishing

questions.stem: Under the Canada Shipping Act, the master is responsible for:
options: Navigation only, while the owner looks after safety
The paperwork and the crew list, and nothing else
Safety of life, the vessel and the environment
The catch and the fishing licence conditions

questions.stem: A man overboard is best approached with the person:
options: On the leeward side
Behind the propeller
On the windward side
In the wake
